newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil union official upbeat on Paranagua talks.
newsitem.headline: Brazil union official upbeat on Paranagua talks.

text.p: A spokesman for dockworkers at the center of a wage dispute at the key Brazilian port of Paranagua was optimistic that a solution could be reached at any moment which would avert a strike on March 5.
"At any moment, a channel of dialogue can be opened," said an official at the dockworkers' union.

Dockworkers and the union of port operators are currently holding talks over the dockworkers' demand for a 21 percent pay increase which they say they are owed since last year, a spokesman for the Paranagua Unions Council (PUC) said.
"Negotiations are taking place between the port operators' union SINDOP and the union of dockworkers," said PUC secretary Nelson Bandeira. "There is a possibility that the strike will be averted."
All Paranagua portworkers have threatened to go on strike on Mar 5 to support the dockworkers' demand for the pay rise which everyone except them received in March 1996.

"They didn't agree to the wage increase at the time because they thought it was too low," said Bandeira. But now the dockworkers wanted the wage rise to be made retroactive, although if port operators agreed to impose the increase effective from March 1 1997, the strike would be called off, he added.

Officials had no specific timetable for a possible agreement which could avert the strike, scheduled to start at 0700 local/1000 GMT on Mar 5. Other portworkers could call a nationwide strike in sympathy on Mar 6 if no deal is struck.
